∡ denotes directed angles modulo 180°. Let M be the midpoint of BC. Let N be the midpoint of AC.

Claim 1. △AHB ∼ △MON.

Proof. ∡HAB = ∡(AH, MN) = ∡OMN (MN is a midline of △ABC; AH ∥ OM, both ⟂ BC). ∡ABH = ∡(MN, BH) = ∡MNO (MN is a midline of △ABC; BH ∥ ON, both ⟂ AC). Hence △AHB ∼ △MON.

∡HAG = ∡OMG (AH ∥ OM, both ⟂ BC). As drawn, AH / AG = AH·MN / (AB·MG) = MO / MG (intercept theorem, AB ∥ MN, MN is a midline of △ABC; Claim 1). Hence △AHG ∼ △MOG.

∡OGH = ∡(OM, AH)    [△AHG ∼ △MOG]
     = ∡OMB + 90°    [AH ⟂ BC]
     = 0°    [OM is the perpendicular bisector of BC]

so O, G, H are collinear. ∎
